rationale: All four of my round-6 asks are confirmed fixed at e7388f71, and the diff from 8b3a5535 introduces no defect in my lens. Skip-and-report for class-(b) placeholders opens no new false PASS: a placeholder never becomes a git operand, it is reported in the output, and the only way an attacker uses it is to rewrite a later unlanded registration's SHA into a placeholder — which is the panel-file-edit reach the residual already states and AC-11 (ix-g) pins (deletion and rewrite are the same reach). Failing closed on placeholders would instead refuse the one legitimate shape in the repo forever (`.mindspec/reviews/6ou2-fix-zfc/panel.json`, bead_id mindspec-6ou2, `reviewed_head_sha: "design-review-no-code"`, the only non-hex value among all tracked bead registrations) with no sanctioned recovery. The class boundaries are sound: anything option-like or carrying revision-expression characters is (d) and fails closed, so a bare `HEAD`, `main`, or a 39-hex string is a skipped placeholder rather than an operand. The plan-blob probe now distinguishes absent from failed with a typed error, and the fifth fixture pins the checkout fallback without a spurious divergence notice.

findings.title: Regression check of git diff 8b3a5535 e7388f71 (adversary lens)
findings.detail: Value classes: (a) empty skipped, (b) placeholder skipped and reported, (c) well-formed evaluated, (d) option-like or revision-expression fails closed. No false PASS is opened: only (c) reaches git; rewriting a later unlanded registration's SHA into a placeholder is the already-stated panel-edit reach (equivalent to deleting the registration), it is reported rather than silent, and it leaves the same no-JSONL-trace residual that (ix-g) pins. Verified the motivating example live: `.mindspec/reviews/6ou2-fix-zfc/panel.json` is `{bead_id: mindspec-6ou2, round: 1, reviewed_head_sha: "design-review-no-code"}` and is the only non-hex `reviewed_head_sha` among all tracked bead-targeted registrations; the repo's only `-rN` directory is `prerelease-r2`, which the spec correctly notes has no bead_id. Class (d)'s character list covers `^ ~ : @{ .. whitespace control` and a leading `-`, so `HEAD~1`, `main^`, `a..b` and `--output=…` fail closed while bare words become skipped placeholders — a safe partition because a bare word can never resolve to a commit through `merge-base` since it never gets there. Plan source: 'exists AND carries the blob' plus the typed `ErrPathNotAtRef` probe (`rev-parse --verify`, `ls-tree`, then the blob read) correctly separates absence from failure; the fifth fixture (branch without a committed plan.md → checkout used, no divergence notice; probe failure → refuse) closes the gap the previous wording left. Residual wording: 'same forge mechanism as Spec-125 item (c), new and bounded reach' is now consistent between the touchpoint and R4.2. Repo-convention re-derivation recipe is reproducible (I re-ran it: zero `-r[0-9]+` directories among bead registrations). Nothing in the diff weakens F1, F3 or F4, the audited tuple, the read-back conditions, or the override fingerprint.
